articles.headline: NBA championship and Finals MVP odds: Thunder remain title favorites heading into Game 7 vs. Spurs
articles.description: Game 7 is set for Saturday in Oklahoma City, with the Thunder-Spurs winner playing the Eastern Conference champion Knicks in the NBA Finals.

images.name: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander [1296x729]
images.caption: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Victor Wembanyama are Nos. 1 and 2 in the Finals MVP odds, respectively.

images.name: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander [608x342]
images.caption: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and the Thunder are back to being odds-on title favorites after taking a 3-2 series lead over the Spurs.
images.alt: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander

images.name: Jalen Brunson [608x342]
images.caption: Jalen Brunson has the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals for the first time since 1999.
images.alt: Jalen Brunson

images.name: Knicks/Cavs [1296x729]
images.caption: The Knicks are looking to end the series against the Cavaliers tonight, as they have the second-shortest title odds and are an overwhelming favorite to win the East.
images.alt: New York Knicks guard Landry Shamet (L) defends Cleveland Cavaliers guard Donovan Mitchell (R) during game 3 of the NBA East Conference Finals between the Cleveland Cavaliers and the New York Knicks in Cleveland, Ohio, USA, 23 May 2026.

images.name: Jalen Brunson [608x342]
images.caption: The Knicks are now heavy favorites to win the Eastern Conference after taking a 3-0 series lead over the Cavs.
images.alt: Jalen Brunson
images.credit: Nathaniel S. Butler/NBAE via Getty Images

images.name: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander  [1296x729]
images.caption: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander how has even odds to win the Finals MVP.
images.alt: Oklahoma City Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (2) takes a shot as San Antonio Spurs guard Stephon Castle (5) defends during the first quarter during game two of the western conference finals for the 2026 NBA playoffs at Paycom Center.

images.name: Victor Wembanyama, Jalen Williams [608x342] - Copy
images.caption: VIctor Wembanyama poured in 41 points and grabbed 24 boards in the Spurs' thrilling Game 1 win.

images.name: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander [1296x729]
images.caption: The Thunder enter the Western Conference Finals as the odds-on favorite to win the NBA championship.
images.alt: Oklahoma City Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (2) looks for an outlet against San Antonio Spurs guard Stephon Castle (5) during the first half of an NBA basketball game, Tuesday, Jan. 13, 2026, in Oklahoma City.

images.name: Cade Cunningham [1296x729]
images.caption: Cade Cunningham and the Pistons are favored heading into Game 7.
images.alt: Detroit Pistons guard Cade Cunningham (2) shoots over Cleveland Cavaliers guard Sam Merrill (5) in the second half during game five of the second round of the 2026 NBA Playoffs at Little Caesars Arena.

images.name: De'Aaron Fox [1296x729]
images.caption: The Spurs took care of business with a big Game 5 win at home against the Timberwolves.
images.alt: De'Aaron Fox #4 & Dylan Harper #2 of the San Antonio Spurs high five during the game against the Minnesota Timberwolves during Round Two Game One of the 2026 NBA Playoffs on May 4, 2026 at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas.

images.name: Jalen Brunson [1296x729]
images.caption: The Knicks advanced Sunday with another blowout victory over the 76ers.

images.name: LeBron James  [1296x729]
images.caption: LeBron James and the Lakers are big underdogs against the defending champion Thunder, and Game 1 only lengthened their odds.

images.caption: The 76ers' odds to win the NBA Finals have marginally shortened after beating the Celtics in seven games.

images.name: Jalen Brunson [1296x729]
images.caption: After entering the playoffs 18-1 to win the NBA championship, the Knicks enter the conference semifinals at 19-1.

images.name: Anthony Edwards [608x342]
images.caption: The loss of Anthony Edwards put a damper on the Timberwolves' championship odds.

images.caption: LeBron James and the Los Angeles Lakers were 150-1 long shots to win the title entering their first-round series against the Houston Rockets.

article.headline: Millsap's floater leads Nuggets to 102-100 win over Pacers
article.description: Paul Millsap hit a left-handed layup with 7 seconds remaining, Nikola Jokic scored 26 points before being ejected in the fourth quarter for arguing and the Denver Nuggets moved to the verge of their first playoff spot since 2012-13 with a 102-100...
article.linkText: Millsap's floater leads Nuggets to 102-100 win over Pacers
article.story: DENVER -- Nikola Jokic has made a habit of bailing the Denver Nuggets out of bad situations. His teammates returned the favor. Paul Millsap hit a left-handed layup with 7 seconds remaining after Jokic was ejected late in the fourth quarter for arguing and the Nuggets moved to the verge of their first playoff spot since 2012-13 with a 102-100 victory over the Indiana Pacers on Saturday night. The magic number for the Nuggets dropped to one as they remained in the No. 2 spot behind Golden State. Denver ran its home record to a Western Conference-leading 30-6. The Nuggets were up 96-89 with 2:56 remaining when Jokic was called for a foul while jostling with Myles Turner. Jokic was incensed at the call and kept barking at official Tony Brothers, who tossed Jokic. Indiana later tied the game at 100, before Millsap hit the winner over Turner. Bojan Bogdanovic's 3-pointer bounced off the rim in the final seconds. "We won," said Jokic, who had a team-high 26 points. "That's the most important thing." Jokic watched Millsap take over on the big screen in the locker room. Millsap finished with 15 points -- nine in the fourth quarter -- and 13 rebounds for Denver, which overcame an 18-point, first-half deficit. "When Nikola got ejected, I went to Paul time and time again," Nuggets coach Michael Malone said. "That's what you want from your guy who's been there and done that. That was a playoff-type game. Paul came through in a big way down the stretch." Thaddeus Young led Indiana with 18 points and 10 boards. The magic number for earning their fourth straight playoff spot stays at one for a Pacers team that hasn't won in Denver since Nov. 27, 2007. This didn't help the Pacers' cause: They were 0 for 11 from 3-point range in the second half. "We were getting good looks," Darren Collison said. "In the playoffs when these things don't go your way you've still got to find a way to win the game. We still had a chance to win the game." Both teams entered the game coming off last-second wins. Wesley Matthews hit a follow shot with 1.8 seconds left in a victory over Oklahoma City on Thursday. Jokic hit a one-handed shot at the buzzer to get by Dallas that same night. This one went down to the wire as well with Jokic's outburst opening the door. Bogdanovic hit the technical free throws and Turner two more for the foul by Jokic. Turner knotted the game at 100 with 27 seconds remaining by hitting one of two free throws. That set the scene for Millsap, who drove in on Turner and just lofted it up. The Nuggets improve to 12-3 this season in games decided by three points or less. "It shows the type of character we have," Millsap said. "Those situations can make or break a team and we've been able to thrive off of it." TIP-INS Pacers: G Tyreke Evans returned after missing three games due to personal reasons and a respiratory infection. He had five points. Nuggets: The teams held a moment of silence for the victims of the mosque shootings in New Zealand. ... Will Barton and Jamal Murray each had 17 points. HIGH EXPECTATIONS The Nuggets have missed the playoffs in each of the last two seasons by a spot. This season, they've left nothing to chance. "We've seen what we're capable of and we're going to hold ourselves to the highest standard possible," Malone said. INCREASED ROLE With Victor Oladipo's season-ending knee injury, the Paces are using Bogdanovic in even more creative ways. "We are putting the ball in his hands and running more pick-and-roll," coach Nate McMillan explained. TECHNICAL FOUL Asked if he deserved to be ejected, Jokic simply responded, "Yes." Asked if he's working on keeping his emotions in check, Jokic elaborated a little more. "It's extremely hard because it's not equal for everybody," Jokic said. PIVOTAL POINT Trailing by as many as 18 points in the second quarter, the Nuggets closed out the half on a 15-2 run. Barton hit a 3-pointer with 1.4 seconds remaining to trim the deficit to 60-57 at the break. UP NEXT Pacers: At Trail Blazers on Monday. They've lost nine straight in Portland. Nuggets: Start a four-game trip Monday in Boston. --- More AP NBA: https://apnews.com/NBA and https://twitter.com/AP-Sports
